name: Needle in a Haystack — Hard
description: COST WARNING: the most expensive test in Gauntlet, about 118k input tokens per case (≈107k with a typical tokenizer) plus long reasoning, so it has only 2 seeds. It needs a context window of at least ~130k tokens. The hard tier is a seeded ~78,000-word chronicle with twelve needles: three single facts, two 2-hop chains, three 3-hop chains with a near-miss decoy at every hop (the look-alike captain, master or ally leads to a different answer), two totals summed from five scattered mentions (with decoys for undelivered shipments, a different commodity from the same source and a look-alike source), and two values corrected later in the text, each shadowed by a look-alike entity. One call, twelve short answers, graded deterministically; hedged answers score zero.
hook: 78,000 words, 12 needles, a decoy at every hop. Can anything read this carefully?
author: Gauntlet Core
